hypothesis.text: Modify `_or_opt` in `policies/baseline_modules/local_search.py` to score each feasible length-1/2/3 inter-route segment relocation using an exact constant-time directed edge delta rather than materializing `src_without` and every destination trial route and recomputing their complete costs. For each source segment, compute its removal gain once from its predecessor/segment/successor boundary arcs and directed internal cost; for each destination position and orientation, compute insertion cost from the destination boundary arcs plus the corresponding forward or reversed segment arcs. Retain the current capacity test, source/destination/position/orientation enumeration, best-gain selection, strict `_EPS` criterion, deadline polling, and route reconstruction/recalculation only after committing the selected improving move. The same fully evaluated route-state transition is therefore selected, including for asymmetric distances, but less VNS scoring work leaves more of the fixed budget for local search and ALNS trajectories.
hypothesis.target_weakness: `_or_opt` currently allocates source/destination trial sequences and recomputes full depot-to-depot route distances for every tested relocation position and orientation, despite only boundary edges and the segment's directed internal edges changing. This repeated linear work occurs in all three high-frequency Or-opt neighborhoods inside a budget-exhausting VNS.
hypothesis.expected_effect: No regression in structural feasibility or fleet_violation; lower VNS scoring overhead, more completed ALNS iterations, and lower final total_distance among equal-fleet feasible outputs.
